speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me exactly when the weakness and numbness started, and did it come on suddenly or gradually? I also need to know if you have experienced any facial drooping, speech difficulties, or weakness in your legs.

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the subacute progression, significant weight loss, and history of substance use, I need to rule out malignancy or severe metabolic complications. REQUEST TEST: MRI_of_the_brain_and_spine.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI is normal, I need to look for peripheral causes. Do you have any pain in your neck, shoulder, or arm, and do you notice any muscle wasting or fasciculations in the right arm?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRI and your history of anabolic steroid use, I suspect a compressive neuropathy like thoracic outlet syndrome or a brachial plexopathy. REQUEST TEST: Nerve_conduction_study_and_EMG.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging and electrophysiology, I suspect a metabolic or systemic cause like steroid myopathy or severe diabetic neuropathy. REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive_metabolic_panel_and_hemoglobin_A1c.

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite normal metabolic panels, the significant weight loss and history of heavy smoking and alcohol use raise concern for a paraneoplastic syndrome or a systemic inflammatory condition. REQUEST TEST: Chest_CTA_and_tumor_markers.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest CT reveals a solid mass at the apex of the right lung, suggestive of a tumor. Tumor markers are elevated, consistent with malignancy.

speaker: Doctor
text: The apical lung mass confirms a Pancoast tumor, which explains your right arm pain, weakness, and sensory loss due to brachial plexus involvement. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast tumor
